title: He led a tribal uprising against colonial exploitation. India now marks his birthday as a national day of pride. November 15, 2026.
excerpt: On Birsa Munda's 151st birth anniversary, observed nationally as Janjatiya Gaurav Divas, the story of the tribal leader whose uprising won a land-rights law that still protects tribal communities today.
bodyHtml:
He led a tribal uprising against colonial exploitation. India now marks his birthday as a national day of pride

Birsa Munda was born on November 15, 1875, in Ulihatu village, present-day Jharkhand. He led the Ulgulan - the "Great Tumult" - a tribal uprising between 1899 and 1900 against British colonial exploitation and the land practices imposed on tribal communities.

His movement forced the colonial government to pass the Chotanagpur Tenancy Act of 1908, protecting tribal land rights - a law that still stands. In 2021, the Indian government instituted his birthday as Janjatiya Gaurav Divas, Tribal Pride Day, honoring tribal freedom fighters nationwide.

Birsa Munda didn't just resist colonial rule - he won a legal protection for tribal land that has outlasted him by more than a century.

sources.text: PIB (Ministry of Tribal Affairs) - Janjatiya Gaurav Divas
